claims.summary: For every exponent pair alpha in [1,infinity]^2 (beta = max_j 1/alpha_j), every N, every level y >= 2 (y <= N if an exponent is infinite) and every N points x_i in [0,1]^2: with r = (2Ny(log(1+y))^beta)^(-1/2), a = yr, G = max_i max(0, a - y|z - x_i|_inf) has cost int sum_j psi*_alpha_j(|d_j G|) <= 2, one partial +-y and the other 0 a.e. where grad G != 0, and sum_i G(x_i) - N int G >= (2/3) N a = (sqrt 2/3) sqrt(N y) (log(1+y))^(-beta/2). So against Lebesgue measure the conjugate class is unbounded for every point set when both exponents are finite, and at least (sqrt 2/3) N (log(1+N))^(-beta/2) when one is infinite (cell smearing is necessary); at (4,4) a Lebesgue bound L' sqrt(N log N) for the functions of level at least y fails for every point set once (sqrt 2/3) sqrt y (log(1+y))^(-1/8) > L' sqrt(log N), e.g. y = (log N)^2.
claims.assessment: Working proof: psi*_alpha(y) <= y (log(1+y))^(1/alpha) for y >= 2 by monotonicity of psi' beyond t_0 = (log(1+y))^(1/alpha); a.e. gradient of a maximum of Lipschitz functions; support area 4Nr^2; pyramid volume 4r^2 a/3.
claims.rationale: Refutes the Lebesgue-measure form of the single-level class bound that the route's lemmas and the fourth route review's outcome (A) targeted, above levels of order log N (log log N)^(1/4) at (4,4); the Lebesgue lemmas stay true but serve there through cell averages, and the smeared X-term reduces to a discrete class on the cells of side delta.
claims.next_action: Split the discrete class (cell averages on the side-delta grid, against centred cell counts) by increment level, a new split not the image of the continuous single-level functions, and bound its single-level part for staircases along curved graphs by curve-trace layers between delta and 2^(-j*(y)); then recombine the levels.

relationships: Shows the cell smearing in the conjecture's class bound is necessary: against Lebesgue measure the class is unbounded for every point set.
Its reduction of the single-level case to the remainder below 2^(-j*(y)) targets a Lebesgue-measure bound that fails at levels (log N)^2.
That lower bound forces the order sqrt(N log N) for random points; this one is deterministic and unbounded, against Lebesgue measure only.
